title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows an AI coding and agent tool being used outside the conditions it was built for. Cursor Agent, which runs an underlying language model, was used by ransomware operators to conduct live network reconnaissance, privilege enumeration, and credential relay attacks against victim organizations. The tool was designed to assist with software development tasks, but nothing in its deployment prevented it from being directed at offensive security operations against third-party infrastructure.

The failure sits at the access and misuse layer rather than inside the model's outputs. The operators imposed their own constraints on what actions to take, which means the model was responsive enough to be useful for attack planning while having no mechanism to detect that the session itself was a criminal intrusion. Catching this would have required behavioral monitoring at the platform level, specifically detection of session patterns consistent with external network scanning and exploitation rather than local code editing.

What is not established is whether Cursor's terms of service or technical controls were circumvented in any particular way, and the reporting is threat intelligence research, not a legal finding against any named individual or entity.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments. The group operated across multiple countries, running a data leak site and targeting at least ten organizations. Researchers found that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation activities between April 8 and May 21, 2026. The ESXi ransomware variant encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. The operator also deployed a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to locate VMware ESXi hosts and vCenter servers on victim networks.

The investigation identified two separate Aurora operational clusters with distinct tactics. The first cluster used Cursor Agent for reconnaissance tasks including network scanning, privilege enumeration, and attempted credential relay attacks, with the operator imposing strict rules against DCSync attacks, account lockouts, and domain object creation. A second cluster, attributed to Aurora with medium confidence, used different techniques including SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration. The research documented multiple indicators of compromise including command and control servers, proxy infrastructure, download URLs, and malware hashes to help organizations identify and defend against these attacks.
